A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work. Their complete text, equations, Table 1, Algorithms 1–3, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports definitions, theoretical constructions, and proofs, but no original empirical results. Appendix B.3 attributes the reported attack measurements to Li, Shen, and Kawaguchi [LSK24].

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical, including its appendices. The retained VA3 measurements are attributed to prior work, and the added prompt example is hypothetical.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the reconstruction construction in Appendix B retain their procedures. Renaming blameless and clean-room 'copy protection' to 'copyright protection' does not change the method.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or tasks actually used in original training or evaluation. The discussed application domains and theoretical dataset examples remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The same NAF/CP, CP-k, VA3, and differential-privacy approaches appear in the theoretical comparisons and prior-work discussion. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an original experimental evaluation protocol. Section 8's numerical parameter examples remain theoretical illustrations with unchanged settings.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies are added or removed. The new prompt example in Section 3.3.1 illustrates the existing theoretical counterexample without testing it.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. The retained probabilistic proof guarantees are not uncertainty estimates for empirical measurements.

E6.justification: Section 8's numerical illustrations and Appendix B.3's cited VA3 amplification figures, including 0.40% to 13.64% and 8.52% to 77.36%, are unchanged. No empirical result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 replaces 'Let k_x ≤ ...' with a guarantee holding 'for some k_x ≤ ...', correcting its quantification and aligning it with the retained Theorem B.4. The principal definitions, constructions, and appendix proofs remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and five contribution statements retain the same central claims about NAF failures, tainted models, blameless and clean-room protection, and differential privacy on golden datasets. The terminology changes do not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 1.1 specifies the US legal framing and explicitly disclaims legal conclusions or an absolute shield against liability. Section 8 strengthens the dataset-dependence caveat from 'not ideal' to 'mostly theoretical interest', while Remark 8.4 explicitly associates possible improvements with additional assumptions.

D1.justification: The pseudocode and technical descriptions are retained. No implementation instructions, code or data access information, experimental hyperparameters, or resource measurements are added or revised.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same 17 works, and substantive comparisons with NAF, VA3, and prior DP/copyright research are retained. Section 1.1's provable-security analogy explains the existing approach without changing novelty claims or those relationships.

P1.justification: v3 adds the legal-terminology subsection, renumbers Notation from 1.1 to 1.2, standardizes 'copyright protection', and makes local explanatory and wording corrections. Most prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Algorithm 3 moves from page 19 to page 21, and Algorithms 1–2 now share page 19 with exposition. Table 1 and the pseudocode displays retain their structure; other visual differences mainly concern text reflow and footnote placement.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Theorem 3.3's quantifier, clarifies that mathematical guarantees do not establish legal immunity, and more clearly acknowledges the DP bound's practical limitations. These improve precision and interpretation while retaining the substantive theory and appendix material. The gains are limited because the main results and underlying feasibility challenges remain unchanged.
